description: A funding source's area-to-volume figure is the mean of each spatial record's area ÷ volume.

b.request: For each funding source, using only spatial records that match a project and have non-null values, calculate the mean of the per-record `(boxy − boxx) ÷ boxx` values and the mean of the per-record `aream2 ÷ volm3` values; return sources whose latter mean exceeds the unweighted average of those source-level means, showing the source, both means, and the difference between the source-level mean and that overall average, without rounding
b.sql:
WITH source_means AS (
  SELECT
    p.fundflux,
    AVG((ss.boxy - ss.boxx) / ss.boxx) AS mean_box_ratio,
    AVG(ss.aream2 / ss.volm3) AS mean_area_volume_ratio
  FROM projects p
  JOIN scanspatial ss ON ss.arcref = p.arcregistry
  WHERE ss.boxy IS NOT NULL
    AND ss.boxx IS NOT NULL
    AND ss.aream2 IS NOT NULL
    AND ss.volm3 IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
), overall_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(mean_area_volume_ratio) AS avg_source_mean_area_volume_ratio
  FROM source_means
)
SELECT
  sm.fundflux,
  sm.mean_box_ratio,
  sm.mean_area_volume_ratio,
  sm.mean_area_volume_ratio - oa.avg_source_mean_area_volume_ratio AS difference_from_overall_average
FROM source_means sm
CROSS JOIN overall_average oa
WHERE sm.mean_area_volume_ratio > oa.avg_source_mean_area_volume_ratio;

a.request: For each funding source (`projects.fundflux`), using the spatial records (`scanspatial`) whose `arcref` matches a project's `arcregistry` and dropping any that don't match, work out two numbers. The first is the average over the records of (`boxy` − `boxx`) ÷ `boxx`. The second is the average over the records of each record's area-to-volume ratio (`aream2` ÷ `volm3`). Ignore missing values. Then take the simple average of that area-to-volume figure across all funding sources. List only the funding sources whose figure is above that average. Show the funding source, the average Y-vs-X difference, the area-to-volume figure, and how far the figure is above the cross-source average, with no rounding.
a.sql:
WITH funding_ratios AS (
  SELECT
    p.fundflux,
    AVG((ss.boxy - ss.boxx) / NULLIF(ss.boxx, 0)) AS avg_y_vs_x_difference,
    AVG(ss.aream2 / NULLIF(ss.volm3, 0)) AS area_to_volume_figure
  FROM projects AS p
  JOIN scanspatial AS ss
    ON ss.arcref = p.arcregistry
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
),
source_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(area_to_volume_figure) AS cross_source_average
  FROM funding_ratios
)
SELECT
  fr.fundflux,
  fr.avg_y_vs_x_difference,
  fr.area_to_volume_figure,
  fr.area_to_volume_figure - sa.cross_source_average AS above_average_by
FROM funding_ratios AS fr
CROSS JOIN source_average AS sa
WHERE fr.area_to_volume_figure > sa.cross_source_average;

c.request: Using the spatial records (`scanspatial`) whose `arcref` matches a project's `arcregistry` and dropping any that don't match, look at each funding source (`projects.fundflux`). For each one, give the average relative difference between `boxy` and `boxx`, computed per record as (`boxy` − `boxx`) ÷ `boxx`, and give its area-to-volume ratio (`aream2` to `volm3`). Ignore missing values. Which funding sources have a ratio above the simple average of that ratio across all funding sources? Show the funding source, the average Y-vs-X difference, the ratio, and how far the ratio is above that average, with no rounding. A funding source's area-to-volume figure is the mean of each spatial record's area ÷ volume.
c.sql:
WITH per_source AS (
  SELECT
    p.fundflux,
    AVG((sp.boxy - sp.boxx) / sp.boxx) AS avg_y_vs_x_difference,
    AVG(sp.aream2 / sp.volm3) AS area_to_volume_ratio
  FROM scanspatial AS sp
  JOIN projects AS p
    ON sp.arcref = p.arcregistry
  WHERE sp.boxy IS NOT NULL
    AND sp.boxx IS NOT NULL
    AND sp.boxx <> 0
    AND sp.aream2 IS NOT NULL
    AND sp.volm3 IS NOT NULL
    AND sp.volm3 <> 0
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
),
with_average AS (
  SELECT
    fundflux,
    avg_y_vs_x_difference,
    area_to_volume_ratio,
    AVG(area_to_volume_ratio) OVER () AS simple_average_ratio
  FROM per_source
)
SELECT
  fundflux,
  avg_y_vs_x_difference,
  area_to_volume_ratio,
  area_to_volume_ratio - simple_average_ratio AS above_average_by
FROM with_average
WHERE area_to_volume_ratio > simple_average_ratio;

d.request: Using spatial records from `scanspatial` whose `arcref` matches a project’s `arcregistry` and excluding nonmatches, group the records by funding source (`projects.fundflux`). For each funding source, compute its area-to-volume figure as the mean of each record’s `aream2 ÷ volm3`, ignoring missing values. Also calculate the mean relative difference `(boxy − boxx) ÷ boxx`, ignoring missing values. Which funding sources have an area-to-volume figure above the simple average of that figure across all funding sources? Show each qualifying funding source, its average Y-vs-X difference, its area-to-volume figure, and how far that figure is above the overall average, with no rounding.
d.sql:
WITH funding_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    p.fundflux,
    AVG(s.aream2 / s.volm3) AS area_to_volume,
    AVG((s.boxy - s.boxx) / s.boxx) AS avg_y_vs_x_difference
  FROM scanspatial AS s
  JOIN projects AS p
    ON s.arcref = p.arcregistry
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
), overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(area_to_volume) AS overall_average
  FROM funding_metrics
)
SELECT
  f.fundflux,
  f.avg_y_vs_x_difference,
  f.area_to_volume,
  f.area_to_volume - o.overall_average AS above_overall_average
FROM funding_metrics AS f
CROSS JOIN overall AS o
WHERE f.area_to_volume > o.overall_average;
